title: Chaos
summary: A family of precise but non-equivalent dynamical notions rather than one universal predicate.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

content.plain: “Chaos” has several rigorous definitions. QEVA should name the definition being used instead of treating the word as self-explanatory.
content.exact: QEVA Protocol 0.2 assigns no universal predicate Chaos(T). A record claiming chaos must identify a contextual criterion (for example a named topological, measure-theoretic, symbolic, or metric definition) and state its hypotheses.
content.example: A map may satisfy sensitive dependence while failing some stronger named chaos criterion.
content.caveat: Popular descriptions such as “random-looking” or “small errors grow” are not by themselves mathematical definitions of chaos.

verification.method: Revision migration checked for exact-reference closure and editorial mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA foundation migration
